title: Stapledon’s Effectiveness Conjecture Holds in Dimension Three and Fails in Dimension Four
content: We disprove Stapledon's effectiveness conjecture in dimension four and prove that it holds in dimension three. Our counterexample is a reflexive lattice polytope with seven vertices and an \( S_3 \)-action. Its equivariant \( h^* \)-series is a polynomial whose quadratic coefficient contains the sign representation with multiplicity -1. We have formalised this counterexample in Lean 4, together with several algebraic and combinatorial steps in the three-dimensional proof. For every lattice polytope of dimension at most three and every finite group of affine lattice symmetries, we prove that polynomiality implies effectiveness. Thus four is the least possible dimension of a counterexample.
